doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: American jazz visitors to Australia
summary: Recalls touring packages with Earl Hines, Wild Bill Davison, Benny Goodman and others, and the New Orleans versus bebop tour with Monk and George Lewis.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was it an event when an American jazz musician would come to town?

Big event. I can remember the first concert I went to was — I mix them up — there were three concerts and I mix them up because they happened so close together, but I remember it was Earl Hines and Bobby Hacket, and Wild Bill Davison and Jon Faddis I think. Would he have been around in ‘72?

All right, Jon Faddis, and gee, who else — Benny Goodman, Zoot Sims. There was one promoter that brought packages out. And just before I’d gotten there there was another package. It was New Orleans versus bebop, in one of those jazz war things, where they brought the Thelonious Monk band and Monk was so out of it he kind of didn’t play for a few weeks, and George Lewis’ band as well. And they toured together. And they’d appear on the same stage. So you’d get people from both camps coming along and sitting in different parts of the auditorium and booing the boppers.

Oh yeah. Oh, you wouldn’t speak to the other side. You’d know by the way you were dressed or, you know, what you were drinking or something. It was crazy. But yeah, any Americans that came to town — the Buddy Rich Big Band, Gary Burton came over, and the Basie Band came over once or twice. But of course, because Australia is so far away if musicians did a tour of Japan, sometimes they’d like go south and include Australia and New Zealand in their package. But we saw a fair bit of good talent, but not as much as I’d like.
